subject: science
intro: Chemical reactions involve breaking the bonds in the reactants and forming new bonds in the products. Breaking bonds absorbs (takes in) energy, and forming bonds releases energy. If forming the new bonds releases more energy than breaking the old bonds absorbed, the reaction releases energy overall and is called exothermic (it gives off heat). If breaking bonds absorbs more energy than forming bonds releases, the reaction absorbs energy overall and is called endothermic (it takes in heat). The net energy change depends on the total bond energy before and after.

items.prompt: In a reaction, forming the new bonds releases more energy than breaking the old bonds absorbed. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?

steps: Breaking bonds absorbs energy and forming bonds releases energy.
Here more energy is released (forming) than absorbed (breaking).
So the reaction releases energy overall, making it exothermic.
solution.answer: Exothermic, because more energy is released forming bonds than was absorbed breaking bonds.

items.prompt: What happens to energy when a bond is broken, and when a bond is formed?

steps: Breaking and forming bonds have opposite energy changes.
Breaking a bond absorbs (takes in) energy.
solution.answer: Breaking a bond absorbs energy; forming a bond releases energy.

items.prompt: A reaction feels cold because it takes in heat from its surroundings. Is it exothermic or endothermic, and what does that say about bond energies?

steps: Taking in heat means the reaction absorbs energy overall.
A reaction that absorbs energy overall is endothermic.
This means breaking the bonds absorbed more energy than forming the new bonds released.
solution.answer: Endothermic, because it absorbs energy; breaking bonds took in more energy than forming bonds released.

items.prompt: Does breaking a bond release or absorb energy?

steps: Bonds hold atoms together, so pulling them apart needs energy.

items.prompt: Burning fuel gives off a lot of heat. Explain in terms of bond energy why it is exothermic.

steps: Burning breaks the bonds in the fuel and oxygen and forms new bonds in the products.
Forming the new bonds releases more energy than breaking the old bonds absorbed.
So there is a net release of energy as heat, making burning exothermic.
solution.answer: Forming the product bonds releases more energy than breaking the fuel and oxygen bonds absorbed, so it is exothermic (releases heat).

items.prompt: Develop a model to compare an exothermic and an endothermic reaction in terms of bond energy.

steps: In both, bonds break (absorbing energy) and new bonds form (releasing energy).
In an exothermic reaction, forming releases more than breaking absorbed, so energy is released overall.
In an endothermic reaction, breaking absorbs more than forming releases, so energy is absorbed overall.
solution.answer: Exothermic: forming bonds releases more than breaking absorbs, so energy is released. Endothermic: breaking absorbs more than forming releases, so energy is absorbed.
